title: Probabilistic shadowing and auto-heal for staggered A/B rollouts
author: Ava Martinez

description:
Context: We need a safer, lower-risk way to evaluate new model variants at scale while preserving service-level guarantees. Existing staged canaries and shadow lanes either duplicate 100% of traffic (expensive) or use static mirrors that are hard to tune for low-volume cohorts. This PR introduces a probabilistic shadowing primitive plus an automatic healing/deprioritization controller designed for staggered A/B rollouts and cohort-aware safety.

Motivation: Reduce cost and noise of shadow evaluation while retaining strong statistical signal across cohorts. Enable automatic graceful degradation of new variants when quality or latency regressions are detected, without immediate blunt rollback. Provide an operationally friendly rollout path that works with Dedicated and Private deployments.

What this PR does (high level): Implements a "probabilistic shadow router" that forwards a sampled fraction p of live requests to a shadow model variant (off the critical path) and records structured deltas. Adds an "auto-heal" controller that continuously evaluates cohort-level metrics (latency p95, token cost delta, and quality delta from a lightweight synthetic eval hook) and: 1) nudges the shadow probability downward for cohorts with sustained negative deltas, 2) activates a temporary deprioritization lane that diverts future traffic to the incumbent model when degradation crosses thresholds, and 3) optionally quarantines the variant for manual triage if regressions persist. This controller supports graceful deprioritization (keep shadowing at a low rate for telemetry continuity) and a fast rollback path when safety gates trip.

Design details: - Router: lightweight policy in the main request router. Sampling uses a seeded hash of request identifiers + cohort id to ensure stable per-user sampling. Sampling rate is configurable per-cohort and can be adjusted by the controller. Shadow requests include a tracing header and are executed under lowered resource priority (batching caps) to avoid interfering with main-line SLOs. - Recorder: compact structured diffs saved to the observation buffer (new compact protobuf schema) and exported to observability pipeline. Deltas include latency_ms, tokens_generated, top-k label differences, and a compact eval score when available. - Auto-heal controller: periodic reconciliation loop that computes rolling windows (5m, 30m) and uses a small decision graph with hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping. Gates configurable via rollout policy: latency_p95 +5% for 30m triggers deprioritization; quality delta below threshold for 1h triggers quarantine. - Rollout integration: rollout manifest accepts new fields: probabilistic_shadow: { cohorts: [{id, initial_rate}], auto_heal: {enabled, thresholds, deprioritization_steps} } - Safety: fallback routes, quota caps for shadow compute, and automatic circuit-breaker to stop shadowing if cluster capacity is constrained.

Checklist (what's included): - [x] Router sampling and seed-stable cohort bucketing - [x] Observation buffer schema + exporter - [x] Auto-heal controller with deprioritization path and quarantine - [x] Rollout manifest schema validation and migration - [x] Unit tests for sampling determinism and controller decision graph - [x] Integration tests in staging that replay production traces against shadow variants - [x] Docs: design doc and user guide for rollout manifest fields - [x] Migration script for manifests with legacy shadowing fields

Testing & validation: - Unit: deterministic sampling, recorder serialization, controller hysteresis logic (mock windows) - Integration: end-to-end on staging with synthetic cohorts (0.1%, 1%, 10%) — exercises deprioritization and quarantine transitions - Perf: microbenchmarks show router overhead <0.7% p95 latency increase at 10% global shadow rate when priority caps applied - Safety: ran a failure-injection canary that caused the controller to deprioritize within expected window; quarantine path held variant out of rotation for manual inspection.

Rollout plan: staged rollout using existing canary pipeline: 0.1% (1d) -> 1% (2d) -> 10% (3d) -> 50% (7d) -> 100%. Auto-heal enabled from day 1 with conservative thresholds. Initial deployment limited to non-critical cohorts (marketing/experimentation groups) and only in regions with capacity headroom.

Operational notes: - New metrics published: rollout.prob_shadow.rate, rollout.auto_heal.actions, rollout.shadow.delta.{latency,quality,cost} - Alerts: default policy triggers when auto_heal performs >3 deprioritizations in 1h or when quarantine rate >0.5% of cohorts. - Conservatively capped shadow compute by default at 10% per-cluster.

Related work: Builds on the shadowing backplane in pkg/rollout; complements the cohort-aware splitters introduced in ENG-92457. See linked Linear tickets for product acceptance criteria.

Why this is different: The probabilistic approach gives predictable telemetry with lower cost and the auto-heal controller provides an intermediate path between blind rollout and immediate rollback, preserving SLAs while surfacing real regressions for ops to act on.

notes_for_ops: If controller performs >3 deprioritizations in 1h open incident and tag teams: runtime + infra. Use /rollouts/inspect?variant=<id> to view compact deltas. To disable probabilistic shadowing globally set rollout.prob_shadow.global_enable=false in values.yaml.
